scope: Read sources for the convention contract; not numerical arc fixtures.

sources.author: Claudius Ptolemy
sources.title: Tetrabiblos
sources.locator: Book III, chapter XIV, printed pages 94-96
sources.excerpt: each equatorial degree being taken to signify one solar year
supports: Equatorial arc to solar-year mapping attributed to Ptolemy.
Proportional temporal-hour construction using the appropriate diurnal or nocturnal hourly times.

sources.author: Placidus de Titis
sources.title: Primum Mobile
sources.locator: Printed pages 17-23, theses 40, 45-46, 55, 60-61; page 57; pages 104-105, canon XXXVII
sources.excerpt: a proportional division of the diurnal and nocturnal arcs, and no other way.
supports: Mundane positions and aspects use proportional diurnal and nocturnal arcs; bodily latitude is retained.
Direct carries the promissor westward to the fixed position of the significator.
Converse applies the significator's rules to the promissor and vice versa.
The author rejects converse directions of angles and converse zodiacal aspects.

sources.author: William Lilly
sources.title: Christian Astrology
sources.excerpt: the apparent diurnall motion of the Sun for the next day and same hour
supports: Ptolemy's degree/year key and Naibod's timing method are discussed separately.
Lilly attributes to Antonius Maginus a key using the Sun's right ascension at birth and at the same hour the following day.
That natal-day right-ascension difference is used as a fixed annual arc.
notEstablished: The exact Naibod rate is deferred to the timing-key milestone.
Maginus's own text was not independently fetched and read.
The passage does not select a modern UTC, UT1 or TT day convention.
